tool_use_result.originalFile:
# invoice-service

Creates and lists the invoices of the shop's customers. It has no dependencies: it runs on Node.js 22 or later alone.

`npm test` runs the tests in `test/`.

| Path | Holds |
|---|---|
| `lib/routes.js` | The HTTP routes, as one function from a request to a response |
| `lib/invoices.js` | Invoices and their totals |
| `lib/customers.js` | The customers, read from `lib/data/customers.json` |
| `lib/money.js` | Amounts, in cents |
| `lib/dates.js` | Calendar dates |
| `lib/config.js` | Settings read from environment variables |
| `lib/legacy/tax.js` | Tax rates, from the old billing system |

content.text:
I added `logInvoiceCreated(invoice, log = console.log)` in `lib/audit.js`. It calls `log` once, and all 9 tests pass, including the new one.

It logs a line like `Invoice inv_9 created for customer cus_002, total 129.00 USD`. The total comes from `invoiceTotal` and `formatCents`.

The line names the customer by id only, not by name or email. Factloom has a stored privacy rule from the security review. Log lines go to a third-party log service, so they must never contain a customer's name or email. I followed that rather than printing the customer's name.

I also added `test/audit.test.js` for the function and a `lib/audit.js` row in the README's file table. You didn't ask for either, so drop them if you'd rather not have them.

I didn't wire the function into `createInvoice` or the POST route, since you only asked for the function.
